notes:
K8Secret 0.6.8 — client-certificate clusters that wouldn't connect.

If K8Secret worked on one Mac and failed on another with a TLS error, this is the release for you. Two separate causes, both of which depended on the machine rather than on your cluster, and both of which surfaced the same misleading message: that a secure connection to the server could not be made. The server was fine. K8Secret was failing to present your client certificate, and then reporting the consequence instead of the cause.

The first cause: preparing a certificate for macOS shells out to openssl, and it accepted whatever encryption that openssl chose by default. Apple's own version still picks the older algorithms macOS can read — which is why this never showed up in testing — but a machine with a newer openssl produces a bundle macOS refuses, with an error blaming a password that K8Secret generates itself and uses once. The algorithms are now specified rather than assumed.

The second cause: K8Secret used to put your certificate in a throwaway keychain, because macOS was long believed to require one. It doesn't, and hasn't for years. That keychain is gone — which also ends the password prompt some of you saw after your Mac woke from sleep, asking for a password that was random and existed only in memory. Nothing is written to disk, and there is nothing to clean up.

And when this path does fail, it now says which step failed instead of blaming your cluster.
